claim: The Taj Mahal is a white marble mausoleum commissioned in 1632 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
source_name: UNESCO World Heritage List - Taj Mahal

claim: The monument is located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India.
source_name: Archaeological Survey of India - Monument List

claim: The Red Fort in Delhi was the primary residence of Mughal emperors from 1648 to 1857.
source_name: UNESCO World Heritage List - Red Fort Complex

claim: The fort hosts the annual Independence Day flag-hoisting ceremony of India.
The Qutb Minar was begun in 1193 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by his successors, standing 72.5 metres tall in Delhi.
source_name: UNESCO World Heritage List - Qutb Minar and its Monuments

claim: The minar and its surrounding monuments form the first garden city complex in India, built by the Delhi Sultanate.
source_name: Archaeological Survey of India - Qutb Minar

claim: The Ajanta Caves comprise thirty rock-cut Buddhist monuments excavated into a horseshoe-shaped gorge on the Waghora River near Aurangabad, Maharashtra.
source_name: UNESCO World Heritage List - Ajanta Caves

claim: The caves are noted for their surviving wall paintings and sculptures, spanning roughly the 2nd century BCE to the 6th century CE.
source_name: Archaeological Survey of India - Ajanta Caves

claim: The Sun Temple at Konark was built in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty.
source_name: UNESCO World Heritage List - Sun Temple, Konark

claim: The temple is designed in the form of a chariot of the sun god Surya with twelve pairs of carved wheels.
source_name: Archaeological Survey of India - Konark Monuments

claim: The Khajuraho Group of Monuments comprises Hindu and Jain temples built between 950 and 1050 CE under the Chandela Dynasty.
source_name: UNESCO World Heritage List - Khajuraho Group of Monuments

claim: The temples are noted for their Nagara-style architecture and elaborate sculptural decoration.
The Elephanta Caves are rock-cut cave temples on Elephanta Island dedicated primarily to Shiva, dating from the 6th to 8th centuries.
source_name: UNESCO World Heritage List - Elephanta Caves

claim: The site includes the celebrated Trimurti (three-headed Shiva) sculptural panel at the main shrine entrance.
source_name: Archaeological Survey of India - Elephanta Caves

claim: Jama Masjid was commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan and completed in 1656 CE.
source_name: UNESCO World Heritage List - Red Fort Complex

claim: The mosque's courtyard can accommodate over 25,000 worshippers, making it one of the largest mosques in India.
